title: First-class provenance metadata on memory records
summary: Add a governed `origin` field (enum: DIRECT_WRITE / EXTRACTION / CONSOLIDATION / RECONCILIATION / INGEST_RESOLVER) to every memory record instead of relying on free-form metadata — foundation for TRU-2's integrity guard.
description: Today no memory record tracks *how* it came to exist as a governed, queryable field — confirmed via grep: `_MemoryBase` in models.py has no `origin`/`provenance` column, and 'source' appears exactly once, as a free-form example key inside a `metadata={}` dict in a docstring, not enforced or typed anywhere. Add a `MemoryOrigin` enum to types.py (`DIRECT_WRITE`, `EXTRACTION`, `CONSOLIDATION`, `RECONCILIATION`, `INGEST_RESOLVER`, mirroring the SDK's five actual write paths: `remember()` called directly, `MemoryExtractor` output, `Consolidator` output, a `Reconciler`-driven supersession, and an `IngestResolver` UPDATE/ADD decision) and an `origin: MemoryOrigin` field on `_MemoryBase` in models.py, defaulting to `DIRECT_WRITE` so existing callers are unaffected. Add migration `0008_provenance.sql` (following the existing numbered pattern in `src/agent_memory_sdk/db/migrations/`, most recently `0007_widen_chunks_source_id.sql`) adding a nullable `origin` VARCHAR column to every memory table with a `DIRECT_WRITE` default, so it's backward-compatible with existing rows per ORC-4's `SchemaPolicy.REQUIRE_EXISTING` attach-mode discipline. Wire every internal call site that constructs a derived record (`_run_consolidator`, the `IngestResolver` dispatch in `remember()`, `Reconciler`-driven supersession writes, `MemoryExtractor` output in `add_messages()`) to stamp the correct `origin` value instead of leaving it at the default. Purely additive — no existing behavior changes, no new required constructor args. Independent of every other story in this epic except TRU-2, which depends on this field existing.
